blocks.text: Maple Ridge Farms: what the ground is and what governs it
Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Water and septic: non-domestic groundwater use (irrigation) requires a water licence under the Water Sustainability Act before the water can lawfully be used; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. Onsite sewage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation and only an Authorized Person (a Professional Engineer or a Registered Onsite Wastewater Practitioner) can design, install, repair, maintain or inspect a sewerage system.

The 500 m² cap comes with a fill cap buyers miss: A principal residence on ALR land built without an ALC application must be 500 m² or less in total floor area AND have no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction. On low, wet lowland ground the fill limit can bind before the floor-area limit does.
Thin rural rows are a warning, not a signal: A farm price built on a rural sub-area "trend" is built on almost no sales.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in Maple Ridge?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in Maple Ridge?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.

faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy a "Maple Ridge farm"?
faq.a: The parcel is bought whole: title, buildings, and the residence rights the ALR rules allow on that parcel.

faq.q: Can I irrigate from a well on the parcel?
faq.a: Only with a water licence: under the Water Sustainability Act, groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a licence and payment of water fees and rentals before lawful use; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. Confirm the licence position for the parcel before offering.

Assume onsite sewage until proven otherwise: a building with indoor plumbing not connected to a community sewer must use an onsite system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, designed / installed / inspected only by an Authorized Person. The City's own A1–A3 checklist also records flood plain status and geotechnical items for agricultural properties — run those checks on any lowland parcel.
